newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses end mixed, Paris hit by jitters.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses end mixed, Paris hit by jitters.

text.p: The Paris bourse ended the day well down on Tuesday, its confidece undermined by pre-election nerves, and the rest of Europe finished in a mixed mood after a thin trading session.

In currencies, the dollar climbed against the yen and recovered against the mark after its sentiment was boosted by a forecast from Germany's six leading economic institutions that the dollar will average 1.80 marks in 1998.

The dollar had earlier made little headway against the mark as the German currency was bolstered by the announcement of the French election, which cast a cloud over progress towards European monetary union.
The fall in Paris stocks was a big surprise after the political uncertainty was cleared away by President Jacques Chirac who last night called snap elections for May-June.

After heavy losses on Monday, French shares rebounded strongly at the start following Chirac's announcement--only to tumble by one percent on the blue chip CAC-40 index at one point. They ended with 0.32 percent losses.

Chirac said the early poll was needed to prepare France for a single European currency and give his centre-right coalition a five-year mandate to reform the state, reduce public spending and cut taxes and welfare charges.
Socialist leader Lionel Jospin said the Socialists too favour the single currency -- but not at the price of an extra bout of austerity.

"The market's a bit afraid of everything though it appears the Right has a good chance of winning, albeit with a smaller majority," one trader said, adding there little chance of the Left taking power.
Brokers said the market would be driven by polls from now until the May 25 first round of voting in the parliamentary election. Run-offs in the two-round poll are set for June 1.
Even if Chirac's conservative RPR party returns with a majority, expectations that the government will push through austerity measures disheartened equity investors.
"If they raise taxes, that will hurt consumption more, and if they cut taxes, it could lead to social unrest because in France it would be viewed as 'the rich getting richer'," a trader said.
Traders said the mood was nervous and few investors were willing to stick their necks out by buying until the political horizon became clearer.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, ended trading with gains of 0.4 percent on the FTSE index but volumes remained light as investors continued to fret about the May 1 election and interest rates.
"The drugs and the oils really saved the day," one senior dealer said. "Otherwise, there wasn't much to get too excited about."
The market managed to shake off early losses which came on the heels of a weaker performance in New York overnight. Wall Street was up nearly 0.6 percent near the European close.
In Frankfurt, stocks traded on the floor ended the session slightly down after investors took profits but the computerised IBIS index registered gains of 0.6 as the session ended.
Traders also said it appeared that the German market was benefiting from the uncertain French political outlook, with some investors apparently shifting funds out of French stocks into the DAX.

On the currency front, the dollar climbed by a pfennig and strengthened against the yen but most traders were sitting tight ahead of this weekend's meeting of the G7 industrialsed nations finance ministers.

"The (German institutions') forecast provided a catalyst for the dollar today, but there is still a lot of apprehension ahead of the G7 meeting," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered here.
"Things were very quiet today except for the dollar/mark forecasts which caught the market short," said one trader at a Japanese bank here.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted at 1.7144 marks and 126.23 yen after ending at 1.7035 and 125.63 in late trading in Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 17.4 points at 4,346.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 finished down 8.0 points at 2,514.67.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 7.25 points at 3,340.33.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $341.65 an ounce, compared to Monday's close of $342.25. Silver was two cents up at $4.76.
